title: Michaelis-Menten Kinetics Measurements of Aldo-Keto Reductases in Murine Tissue
author: Morgenstern, Kliemank, et al.

steps.title: Perfuse mice with PBS
steps.instruction: Perform vascular perfusion of each mouse through the heart using 1× PBS to clear blood from tissues.

steps.title: Harvest and snap‑freeze tissue
steps.instruction: Excise the desired tissues, immediately snap‑freeze them in liquid nitrogen after extraction, and store at –80 °C until processing.

steps.title: Pre‑cool grinding tools
steps.instruction: Place a mortar and pestle in a –80 °C freezer for at least 4 h before use.

steps.title: Prepare cold reagents
steps.instruction: Keep liquid nitrogen on hand for cooling materials during grinding and pre‑cool the lysis buffer at 4 °C or on ice throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Set up homogenisation supplies
steps.instruction: For each sample, ready a 1 mL syringe fitted with a 20‑gauge needle; keep all syringes and needles chilled.

steps.title: Homogenise tissue in lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer frozen tissue to the pre‑cooled mortar, add cold lysis buffer, and grind thoroughly while maintaining the material on ice or in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Pre‑cool centrifuge rotors
steps.instruction: Place the centrifuge rotors in a 4 °C environment (refrigerated or on ice) before loading the lysates.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysates
steps.instruction: Spin the homogenised samples at the appropriate speed (as defined by your downstream assay) using the rotors pre‑cooled at 4 °C; collect the supernatant for the enzyme assay.

steps.title: Set up enzyme assay
steps.instruction: Load the supernatant into a microplate (preferred) or cuvettes for a thermostatic spectrophotometer; equilibrate the instrument to 37 °C and keep it there for the entire assay.

steps.title: Measure kinetic data
steps.instruction: Record absorbance (or other read‑out) over time to generate Michaelis‑Menten curves for the aldehyde substrate in each tissue sample.

steps.title: Fit kinetic curves in GraphPad
steps.instruction: Import the raw data into GraphPad Prism, apply a nonlinear regression (least‑squares) fit to the Michaelis‑Menten model, and obtain Km and Vmax values for each substrate‑tissue combination.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Follow the additional instructions provided at https://www.graphpad.com/guides/prism/7/curve-fitting/reg_example_enzyme_kinetics.htm for calculating means, SD, and significance across replicates.

description: This protocol is a straightforward method to determine enzyme kinetics of AKR converted aldehydes in tissue lysates within 4 h. Tissues have to be obtained from mice after vascular perfusion with 1× PBS through the heart and the samples should be snap-frozen after extraction. For tissue processing/crushing, a mortar and pestle needs to be precooled for at least 4 h in a −80°C freezer. Liquid nitrogen is required in order to cool down the materials during the processing. In addition, the lysis buffer should be precooled at 4°C or on ice during the processing. A 1 mL syringe and 20-gauge needle should be prepared for each individual sample and centrifuge rotors should to be precooled at 4°C. For the enzyme assay it is recommended to use a microplate reader but in theory the assay can be run in cuvettes as well using a thermostatic spectrophotometer. Instruments should be kept at 37°C during the assay.
